conflict_topics: location of prayer (room vs living room)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concrete reasons (presentations, exams, ritual timing) and propose concrete mitigation steps (no singing on certain days, moving location, earplugs).
Agent D consistently states a principled constraint about timing and place of prayer, which grounds their resistance.
Some repetition occurs (reiterating 'can't just not do my prayers' and worries about thin walls), but exchanges progress through proposals.
evaluation.final_reason: Agent D agreed to stop using the bell but explicitly refused to stop singing, to perform the prayer at a different time, or to relocate it from their room ('the singing is the actual prayer... it has to be at that time' and 'it's supposed to be in my own space'). Roommates proposed limited requests (no singing on Monday mornings), relocating to the living room, carrying the prayer setup, and earplugs, but D rejected relocation and moving the shelf and only offered to 'try to be as quiet as I can.' No mutually accepted concrete arrangement was reached, so the fundamental incompatibility between D's time-fixed, in-room religious observance and others' weekday sleep needs remains.
position_change_notes: Agent D softened slightly by offering to stop using the bell and to 'try to be as quiet as I can' (Turn 2, Turn 4), but refused to move the ritual or omit singing (Turn 5: 'I can't just not do my prayers'; Turn 9: 'it's a personal prayer... in my own space').
Agent A moved from complaint to proposing specific compromises (no singing on Mondays; moving to living room) and expressed resignation when no solution was accepted (Turn 16: 'So we're stuck').
Agent B proposed practical help and earplugs as mitigations (Turns 17, 19) and later doubted their sufficiency along with A (Turn 22/23).
Agent C initially raised proximity concerns and later broadened the scope, clarifying the impact is 'every weekday morning' (Turn 26).

round_scores.evidence: Agent A: 'I really can't be awake from 4:45 on those days.' Agent D: 'It's a religious observance... The bell is the loudest part, I can stop using it.' (A complaint about waking vs D's intention to continue observance; D offers partial concession on the bell only.)

Agent A: 'How about just on Monday mornings, could you not sing?' Agent B: 'I have a similar issue... my exams are on Tuesdays and Thursdays.' (More household members report incompatible morning needs, widening the dispute.)

Agent D: 'the singing is the actual prayer for me... it has to be at that time, before sunrise.' Agent B: 'On Tuesday and Thursday mornings, could you sing very quietly?' (D insists the singing is essential and time-fixed, resisting requests.)

Agent C: 'My room is right next to yours... Even without the bell, I'm worried any singing... will still wake me.' Agent D: 'I already said I won't use the bell... I'll try to be as quiet as I can.' (D repeats limited concession; others remain concerned.)

Agent A: 'I'm only asking about the four Monday mornings. Can we find a solution just for those specific days?' Agent D: 'What other solution is there?... I can't just not do my prayers.' (A narrows request; D refuses to stop praying.)

Agent A: 'What about the living room, just for the Monday mornings?' Agent B: 'That sounds like it might work.' (Housemates propose a concrete accommodation — moving location — indicating attempt to reduce conflict, though not yet accepted by D.)

Agent D: 'My prayer shelf is in my room. It's not something I can just move to the living room every morning.' Agent A: 'But that still leaves me... "Quiet" singing is still singing right next to my room.' (D rejects the living-room proposal; incompatibility persists.)
Agent D: 'I don't know. I've already told you what I can do. I can't just not do my prayers.' Agent A: 'So we're stuck then.' (Positions remain opposed with no new resolution.)

Agent B: 'What if we help you? On Monday and Thursday mornings, we could help you carry what you need to the living room.' Agent D: 'Thanks... it's not about the carrying. It's a personal prayer. It's supposed to be in my own space.' (Offer to assist is explicitly refused.)

Agent B: 'So what if Agent A and I use earplugs on those mornings?' Agent C: 'The earplugs might work, but I'd need them every single morning.' (A mitigation strategy is proposed that could reduce practical incompatibility, though uncertain.)
Agent A: 'I'm not sure earplugs will be enough, honestly.' Agent B: 'You're probably right.' (Doubts about the proposed mitigation revive the core incompatibility.)
Agent A: 'Right. So we're back to the original problem.' Agent C: 'It's not just Monday. For me, it's every weekday morning.' (Scope of affected parties increases; disagreement remains unresolved.)

substantive_insights: Conflict hinges on an absolute timing/place requirement for the ritual (D) versus household members' fixed morning obligations (A,B,C).
Partial concessions (stopping the bell) are insufficient because the singing itself and its fixed timing are the core incompatibility.

Feasible mitigations (living-room relocation, help carrying, earplugs) fail because of ritual constraints or doubts about effectiveness; the problem thus requires either a change in practice, a household rule negotiation with a clear trade, or acceptance of recurring harm by some members.
